title: Docs Import
summary: Stage source material, review the import decisions, and write it into a configured Docs Viewer collection.
content_html:
Docs Import

Docs Import turns staged source material into canonical Markdown documents and associated media. It runs inside Docs Viewer management and can target a top-level scope or a configured one-level sub-scope collection.

For a top-level scope, open /docs/?scope=<scope> and choose the main Import action. For a configured sub-scope, open its local Manage report and choose the compact 📥 Import action beside New and Actions.

Workflow

The browser presents choices. The local Docs Viewer service resolves staged paths, validates targets, creates the authoritative plan, performs writes, and rebuilds published payloads.

Stage The Source

Put source material in the shared drop-zone:

$DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/data-sharing/import-staging/

Ordinary document sources must be direct children. A Markdown package is a direct-child folder containing one Markdown file plus its local images or attachments. A complete edited Docs Review source/ folder is also staged as one direct-child folder, but uses a separate trusted collection recognizer before generic Markdown handling. The picker shows only formats the server currently accepts; standalone raster, SVG, Mermaid .mmd, and download sources belong to the source editor's Add image… and Add file… actions. Docs Import Architecture owns the format-adapter boundary, while HTML Import Mapping documents the current semantic conversion rules.

Docs Import always creates the target document front matter. For an ordinary Markdown source, a well-formed leading front-matter block is stripped after trusted collection recognition. Its scalar title may be used only when the body has no H1; every other field is ignored with a warning. Malformed or unterminated apparent front matter blocks the import instead of becoming body text.

Import Documents

Use Documents for Word .docx, HTML, Markdown, text, and ordinary Markdown packages. Document packages contains trusted returned JSON/JSONL packages and complete edited review-source folders. Standalone raster, SVG, and downloadable files are not Docs Import sources.

  1. Select one or more staged sources.
  2. Choose the target scope, or confirm the fixed collection label when Import was opened from a sub-scope report.
  3. For HTML, decide whether obvious prompt/meta sections belong in the document.
  4. Choose Import selected.
  5. Inspect the result and open the imported document.

Sub-scope Import fixes the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection as the destination. The scope and import-type controls are disabled. Its package lane shows only returned packages and edited review-source folders whose trusted provenance identifies that exact opted-in collection; checked report rows are not inputs.

Multi-file runs process the selected files in list order. A failure stops the run; successfully completed earlier imports remain. A top-level run refreshes its index. A sub-scope run refreshes only the owning report manifest and opens the final successful child target.

HTML can supply the title; Markdown uses its first H1 when present. Word uses the mapped Title style and falls back to the humanized staged filename without promoting its first section heading. Word Import Style Mapping owns the exact Word heading rules. The staged name remains source context. A genuinely new document receives an immutable local doc_id and matching Markdown filename when the service plans the write.

Every ordinary source import creates a new document with a fresh immutable identity. Importing the same staged file again creates another independent document; the workflow does not scan target documents or offer document overwrite. New documents in public scopes are created non-viewable so they can be checked in management mode before publication.

Create-Only Document Imports

Ordinary Word, HTML, Markdown, text, and Markdown-package sources are intake material, not update identities. Their staged filenames and titles remain conversion context only. Update an existing canonical document through the source editor or another workflow that explicitly identifies that document; ordinary import never infers an update from a filename or title.

This create-only rule does not remove collision handling from returned collections or stable-name assets. Trusted collection records carry explicit document identities: matching canonical identities are planned as overwrites and new records receive local create identities. Role-marked interactive HTML companions retain explicit asset replacement confirmation.

Import A Trusted Collection

Use Document packages for either a trusted returned documents package or a complete edited Docs Review source folder. Review package is optional: it prepares the separate read-only Docs Review projection but does not open or preselect Import. Return to Docs Viewer and choose its normal Import Action.

The server recognizes both collection formats before ordinary Markdown or generic JSON/JSONL handling. A standalone reviewed Markdown file is rejected with guidance to stage and select the complete source folder. Missing, extra, duplicate, malformed, unsafe, or invalid records block either collection as a whole. There is no record selection, skip, or partial apply.

The collection path is deliberately plan-first:

  1. Choose the package and target scope.
  2. Review every record, parent resolution, warning, and blocker.
  3. Review the server-planned creates and overwrites for the complete package.
  4. Confirm the complete package, or cancel without writing.

The plan covers the whole collection. A package record that creates a document receives a planned local identity; the package identifier remains source provenance and parent references are remapped to the local identities. A record matching an existing canonical identity is planned as an overwrite. There is no subset selection, record skip, replacement doc_id, or Create as new choice. Missing undeclared parents, hierarchy cycles, unsafe identities, invalid records, and package-shape errors block confirmation.

For returned JSON/JSONL, content, summary, parent_id, and viewability are planned together. Creates receive fresh local identities; matching canonical identities are overwrites. Omitted body or permitted metadata preserves its current value.

For an edited review-source folder, the displayed name is <review_folder_id> (reviewed) but requests retain the exact staged folder identity. Trusted export metadata and the retained review manifest must prove return-Import capability, exact membership, original scope or configured sub-scope, and prepared source_last_updated values. The folder is overwrite-only: every doc_id must already exist in that exact collection. Edited body, title, and summary may apply. Immutable identity, added_date, review transport fields, and destination-owned group, ui_status, hierarchy, and child visibility do not.

On confirmation the service rereads the selected collection and recomputes its target plan. Changed package/folder hashes, prepared versions, planned actions, hierarchy, or blockers return a refreshed non-writing plan for reconfirmation.

Returned JSON/JSONL apply remains synchronous and partially durable: a source-write failure preserves earlier writes and leaves later records not attempted; generation failure does not undo successful source changes. Edited review-source apply is intentionally atomic. It validates and prepares every overwrite, rechecks the complete canonical snapshot inside the owning scope or sub-scope boundary, writes and rebuilds once, and restores the complete source snapshot and projection after any write or rebuild failure.

Optional Edited-Source Workflow

  1. Prepare a reviewable returned package and open it in Docs Review.
  2. Open exact package sources in VS Code, edit them, and choose Build.
  3. Visually accept the complete retained preview.
  4. Copy the complete package source/ folder into Import staging.
  5. Select its (reviewed) entry, inspect the exact overwrite plan and derived-Markdown fidelity warning, then confirm once.

Steps 1–3 are optional for ordinary returned-package Import. Docs Review never applies canonical changes and its Build endpoint never advances source or canonical timestamps.

Media And Companion Assets

Media behavior comes from the target scope configuration:

  • each logical media type selects its configured published location
  • repository, external-local, and R2 locations use the same provider-independent import plan
  • the chosen provider must complete and byte-verify the media write before canonical source is committed

Markdown packages convert supported images to readable, 800px-maximum WebP outputs and copy supported attachments unchanged. HTML and Markdown can extract inline raster data URLs, and HTML-inline SVG is sanitized and published as deterministic image media. Word imports pass embedded PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP through the same inline-raster publication path; missing alt text receives a deterministic Word image NN label, while unsupported, unreadable, or empty images are omitted with warnings. Exact paths, location providers, collision rules, and media limitations belong to Media Handling.

A standalone HTML file marked with:

<meta name="dlf:docs-import-role" content="interactive-html">

is treated as a companion asset rather than a selectable source. A normal document import copies marked companions directly to the target scope's configured published html root after any required overwrite confirmation. Add the resulting html-media token to the document manually; import does not decide where the sandboxed iframe belongs.

Results And Recovery

An ordinary result identifies the created document, exact parent or child target, Source action, media actions, and conversion warnings. A collection result presents created, overwritten, failed, and not-attempted records directly in the terminal modal. A successful edited review-source result contains overwrites only and reports its atomic rollback state. Docs Import does not create a separate result document or result-specific log.

The terminal result remains in the modal until Close. Reopen the modal to refresh the staged-source list and start another run.

An ordinary one-source failure leaves the selected staged source and destination in place so that source can be retried. After a partial multi-file run, select only failed or unattempted sources; retrying a completed create makes another independent document. If the source write succeeded but the target projection or Source presentation failed, do not import again: use the committed exact target to retry only that presentation step.

Docs Import is best-effort conversion. Normal prose, headings, lists, links, simple tables, Markdown, and supported media are reliable inputs. Word layout, presentation-heavy HTML, interactive UI, unresolved package links, and unsupported assets may need source editing after import. Conversion HTML and inline media bodies remain inside the local service; the generated canonical Markdown is always checked by the shared Python renderer before a source write.

For implementation boundaries, extension methods, and known structural weak spots, see Docs Import Architecture.
